Title: Highfield Therapy
Welcome: Welcome to Highfield Therapy. A warm, confidential space for adults who want to understand old patterns and feel more secure in themselves and their relationships, online or in person in Sheffield. Robert Highfield, MNCPS (Accred).
Situation: From the outside, life may look fine. You're getting on with work, family and responsibilities. But inside you may feel numb, on edge or quietly dissatisfied, and you're not sure why.
Problem: You might find it hard to trust people or feel close to them. You notice yourself falling into the same patterns in relationships, and you know you want to change them, but it keeps happening. Perhaps anxiety or low self-worth follows you around.
Implication: These patterns can repeat themselves in friendships, partnerships and at work, and can slowly narrow what feels possible for you.
Payoff: Therapy offers a steady, confidential space to understand where these patterns began and to build safer, more secure ways of relating, to others and to yourself. The aim is to feel more grounded, more able to trust, and less ruled by old habits.
About: My name is Robert, and my path into therapy grew out of eighteen years working in further education — first as a performing arts lecturer, then supporting students' wellbeing, progression and personal development. It was through that work, and through volunteering as a listening Samaritan and with Cruse Bereavement, I decided to study over three years to become an accredited counsellor. My first work as a counsellor was with the Snowdrop Project Charity, supporting survivors of trafficking and modern slavery; it was there that I found my real calling in walking alongside people through their most difficult experiences. Today I work in private practice as a counsellor and as a trainee psychotherapist in higher education. I hold professional diplomas in counselling and hypnotherapy, alongside extensive safeguarding and mental health first aid training. I believe that emotional wounds are formed in relationships and healed within one. My work is grounded in cultural humility; I see wellbeing as connected not only to the individual but also to family, community, and the wider world around us. I welcome all individuals, regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation or background, by prioritising an affirming, non-judgemental space. Away from the therapy room, you'll usually find me running or out walking.

My name is Robert, and my path into therapy grew out of more than fifteen years in education, first as a performing arts lecturer, then supporting students' wellbeing, progression and personal development across several colleges in Sheffield and beyond. It was through that work, and through volunteering as a listening Samaritan and with Cruse Bereavement and the Snowdrop Project, that I found my real calling in walking alongside people through their most difficult experiences. Today I work in private practice and as a student counsellor at the University of Sheffield. I am an NCPS Accredited counsellor, MNCPS (Accred), and a member of the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy (BACP) and the UK Association for Transactional Analysis (UKATA), with extensive safeguarding and mental health first aid training. I believe that emotional wounds are formed in relationship and healed within one too, and my work is grounded in cultural humility: I see wellbeing as connected not only to the individual but to family, community and the wider world around us. I welcome all individuals, regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation or background, and I'm a committed ally, prioritising an affirming, non-judgemental space for clients from LGBQ+ and Trans communities. Away from the therapy room, you'll usually find me running or out on the golf course.
Therapy: I work in an integrative, trauma-informed way, with a focus on Transactional Analysis (TA). Rather than following a single rigid method, I tailor our work gently and safely to your goals, so you feel grounded and in control. Sessions take place online, or in person in my private Garden Room in Sheffield, a calm space designed to feel like a secure retreat.
Fees: The first step is a free 15-minute phone call. It's a chance to tell me a little about what has brought you here, ask any questions about therapy, and see whether we feel like a good fit, with no commitment. If we both feel it's right, we'll book an in-person or online session. Sessions are £50, with concessions for those on a low or no income.
Contact: I'm based in Sheffield, a 20-minute walk from Sheffield Central station and close to a tram stop, with plenty of free on-street parking. To arrange your free call, phone or message 07946827431, or use the email button below.
